issues.legal_issue: A rent-arrears claim may be established by a tenant’s admissions and other undisputed evidence even when an unregistered lease document cannot be relied on to prove the claimed rent.
material_facts: The suits sought recovery of rent arrears, and the tenant did not dispute the landlord-tenant relationship.
The tenant admitted that annual rent was payable at a stated rate and that rent had not been paid for the claimed period.
The trial court found on the evidence that the tenancy was with the landlord, and the lower appellate court affirmed its findings.
The High Court set aside the decrees solely because the unregistered rent document could not be admitted to support the claim.
issues.conclusion: The High Court could not dismiss the rent claims solely because the lease document was unregistered. The tenant’s admissions and the other evidence established liability for arrears, and the decrees were restored with the amount modified in accordance with the admitted rent.
issues.legal_principle: Under the second paragraph of Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act, a lease may be created by an oral agreement accompanied by delivery of possession, and an unregistered instrument does not prevent the court from finding that a lease and a landlord-tenant relationship existed on other evidence. A party’s admission in pleadings or orally is the best evidence and needs no further corroboration. Applying Anthony v. K.C. Ittoop & Sons, the Court held that the relationship and rights could be determined from undisputed facts despite excluding the unregistered document; Kaladevi v. V.R. Somasundaram was distinguished because it concerned a document used collaterally in a specific-performance suit.

rule.if: rent_arrears_case and landlord_tenant_relationship_undisputed and tenant_admitted_rent_rate and tenant_admitted_nonpayment

predicates.rent_arrears_case: The proceeding seeks recovery of rent said to be unpaid by a tenant.
predicates.landlord_tenant_relationship_undisputed: The parties do not dispute that one is the landlord and the other is the tenant.
predicates.tenant_admitted_rent_rate: The tenant admitted the rate of rent payable.
predicates.tenant_admitted_nonpayment: The tenant admitted that rent was not paid for the period claimed.

issues.definition: When a rent-arrears case involves an undisputed landlord-tenant relationship and the tenant admits both the rent rate and nonpayment, the rent-arrears claim is established.

issues.legal_issue: An unregistered lease document offered to prove the lease terms and rent that form the basis of a rent-arrears claim cannot be treated as evidence merely for a collateral purpose.
material_facts: The suits sought arrears of rent, and the unregistered document was relied on to establish the lease, its terms, and the rate of rent.
The document was offered to support the principal rent claim, not to prove a separate collateral transaction.
The appellants argued that the document could be relied on for a collateral purpose.
issues.conclusion: The collateral-purpose argument was rejected. The unregistered document could not be used to prove the lease terms or rent forming the basis of the claim, though the arrears could be established through the tenant’s admissions and other evidence.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 17 and 49 of the Registration Act, read with Section 107 of the Transfer of Property Act, prevent an unregistered instrument from proving the transaction and terms for which registration is required, while the proviso to Section 49 permits specified collateral use. In Kaladevi v. V.R. Somasundaram, an unregistered sale deed could be received in a specific-performance suit as evidence of an oral agreement of sale, a collateral transaction. That case did not apply because the rent document here was offered to prove the main claim and rent terms. The Court also relied on Anthony v. K.C. Ittoop & Sons concerning the effect of an unregistered lease document.

predicates.rent_arrears_case: The proceeding seeks recovery of rent said to be unpaid by a tenant.
predicates.unregistered_lease_document_offered_for_: A party offers an unregistered lease document to prove the lease terms or rent that form the basis of the claim.

issues.definition: In a rent-arrears case, an unregistered lease document offered to prove the terms underlying the main claim is not admissible to prove those terms.

issues.legal_issue: A challenge to a remittal in rent-control proceedings does not warrant a direct eviction order when proceedings after remittal have taken place and the related appeal remains available to determine the parties’ remedies.
material_facts: A tenant challenged an eviction order, and the High Court remitted the rent-control matter for a decision after allowing the tenant to file a written statement.
After remittal, the Rent Controller dismissed the eviction application, and an appeal from that dismissal was pending before the District Judge.
The petitioners asked the Supreme Court to direct eviction in light of its decision in the rent-arrears appeals.
issues.conclusion: The Court declined to order eviction directly and left the petitioners to pursue their remedies in the pending rent appeal. The special leave petition challenging the remittal was dismissed as infructuous following the post-remittal rent-control proceedings.
issues.legal_principle: The Court declined to bypass the pending rent-control appeal by ordering eviction through a shortcut based on the decision in the rent-arrears appeals. In light of the subsequent proceedings before the Rent Controller, the challenge to the remittal had become infructuous; the parties were left to pursue their remedies in the pending appeal.

predicates.rent_control_remittal_challenge: The proceeding challenges a decision remitting a rent-control matter for further proceedings.
predicates.post_remittal_controller_proceedings_com: The rent-control authority has acted on the remittal and issued a decision.
predicates.related_rent_appeal_pending: An appeal concerning the post-remittal rent-control decision remains pending.

issues.definition: When a challenge to a rent-control remittal is followed by a decision after remittal and a related appeal remains pending, the remittal challenge is infructuous and the eviction issue is left to that appeal.
